title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 10
summary: Oil embarked on a steady climb higher as Iran and Oman remained short of a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, while European diesel prices surged following an attack on a Saudi Arabian refinery near the Red Sea.

title: IBM Raises C$2.75 Billion in First Canada Bond Sale Since 2012
summary: International Business Machines Corp. sold C$2.75 billion ($1.97 billion) of Canadian corporate bonds Monday, building on a record year of issuance in the currency by foreign firms.

title: Iran Doing Good Job of Rattling Trump, Says Bernard Haykel
summary: Professor Bernard Haykel said that President Trump has to be much cooler around negotiations with Iran, as the Iran's government is succeeding at 'rattling' the US president. Haykel, who teaches at Princeton, said that Iran cannot keep sole control of the Strait of Hormuz because that would let them keep the world 'over a barrel.'  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Fed’s Hammack Says ‘Some Number’ of Rate Hikes May Be Needed
summary: Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland President Beth Hammack said it’s possible a number of interest rate hikes may be needed to bring inflation down to the central bank’s 2% target, but she does not want to prejudge what the end point will be.

title: US Natural Gas Surges as Hotter Outlooks Trigger Short-Covering
summary: US natural gas futures closed higher, earlier rising by the most in more than two months, as an unusually large swing in weather forecasts triggered a wave of short-covering among money managers who were the most bearish on gas since 2020.

title: Yen Weakens 1%, Erases Half of US-Japan Intervention Gains
summary: The yen extended its losses, erasing half of the gains triggered when authorities from the US and Japan intervened in the foreign-exchange market to support the currency.

title: Test Your ETF Knowledge In Our IQ Test
summary: Bloomberg's Isabelle Lee puts Eric Balchunas, Jon Maier, chief ETF strategist for JPMorgan Asset Management, and Mayuranki De, vice president of ETF trade strategy at Raymond James, to the test on "Bloomberg ETF IQ" in this week's edition of "IQ Test." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Stocks Churn as Hormuz Standoff Spurs Rally in Oil: Markets Wrap
summary: A rally in oil prices left stocks wavering while bond yields climbed, with trader anxiety building just days ahead of key inflation reports.

title: Deadly Earthquake Hits Colombia
summary:
A deadly earthquake hit Colombia on Monday morning, toppling buildings, burying people under rubble and causing dozens of deaths in the Pacific region and the central Andes.

 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: JBS Returns Leadership to Batista Clan as Scion Named Next CEO
summary: The world’s largest meat supplier, JBS NV, will be led once again by a member of Brazil’s Batista family, a pivotal move for a global food powerhouse that’s increasingly focused on the US.

title: Avantis ETF Cracks Small-Cap Code
summary: Eduardo Repetto, CIO of Avantis Investors, joins Isabelle Lee and Eric Balchunas on "Bloomberg ETF IQ." They discus the Avantis U.S. Small Cap Value (ticker: AVUV). (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Chile Gives Struggling Copper Giant Codelco a $2.4 Billion Boost
summary: Chile’s government will allow state-owned Codelco to retain all of its 2025 profit, leaving about $2.42 billion in the copper giant as it looks to revive production and ease a record debt burden.

title: Largest Private School Bond Deal in Two Years Hits Muni Market
summary: A performing arts school in the heart of Los Angeles is planning to borrow $117 million in the municipal bond market on Tuesday, marking the largest private school deal in two years.

title: Shipping Traffic Is Up Despite War in Iran, Says FreightWaves CEO
summary: Craig Fuller, CEO of FreightWaves, sees stronger trucking, rail and container volumes despite higher shipping and insurance costs because of the war in Iran. He also talks about a new shipping route that is being used to get through the Arctic to avoid the Strait of Hormuz. Fuller speaks on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Saudis Delay Restart of Jazan Plant to Late August, IIR Says
summary: Saudi Aramco pushed back restarting its Jazan oil refinery to late August, following a weekend attack on the facility, according to market intelligence firm IIR Energy.

title: Wheat Climbs With USDA Seen Tightening Global Grain Supply
summary: Wheat was higher as traders braced for the US Department of Agriculture’s monthly supply demand report that’s expected to show declining domestic and world grain supplies.

title: The Other Way to Reduce Government Debt
summary: Financial repression.

title: US Stocks ‘Directionless’ as Chipmaker Earnings, CPI to Set Pace
summary: US stocks were looking for direction after a strong earnings week as investors continue to navigate the uncertain path of interest rates and war in Iran. The market is gearing up for the final stretch of corporate earnings, with chipmakers set to provide confirmation for the long-winded debate over valuations.

title: Iran’s Oil Terminals Look Idle as US Keeps Up Naval Blockade
summary: Iran’s oil terminals have appeared largely idle this month as the US continues to impose a blockade aimed at pressuring the country into a peace deal, though visibility into its operations remains patchy.
